newsitem.title: USA: U S WEST cellular group settles suit.
newsitem.headline: U S WEST cellular group settles suit.

text.p: U S WEST NewVector Group, a cellular communications provider in 12 states, Thursday agreed to settle a lawsuit over its billing methods, resulting in an $8.0 million payment to its 893,000 customers.
U S West NewVector is a unit of U S West Media Group, which is one of two major business groups comprising telecommunications giant U S West Inc.
The class action lawsuit alleged NewVector did not disclose its practice of calculating airtime charges based on rounding to full minutes during the period July 1, 1994, through May 1, 1996.
As part of its settlement, U S West NewVector denied any wrongdoing and said it would rather work with subscribers than pursue "costly" litigation.

Current current customers will receive a credit to their account. Former customers will receive a monetary payment or, if they resubscribe, may receive a waiver of the activation charge and a credit to their account.
